+# A power-mean counterexample in the Euclidean operator norm
+
+## Abstract
+
+An exact positive definite pair violates the p=2 power-mean distance monotonicity in the Euclidean induced operator norm.
+
+Raluca Dumitru and Jose Franco, On the monotonicity of weighted power means of matrices, arXiv:1701.07023v1, Conjecture 9, asks for decreasing distance for every unitarily invariant norm and every 0<p≤2. Version 2 withdraws the preprint because Proposition 4 is false; withdrawal alone does not refute Conjecture 9. The public three-author manuscript of the 2017 successor does not state this exact all-norm assertion. Its p=2 Frobenius and p=1/2 all-unitarily-invariant-norm results are compatible with this counterexample. Publisher full text was not obtained, so no complete version-of-record comparison is claimed. The result here concerns the v1 assertion through its p=2 operator-norm specialization. No exact prior refutation was found in the bounded later primary literature inspected through 2026-11-01; the relevant 2018 The matrix power means and interpolations (DOI 10.15352/aot.1801-1288) remained text-inaccessible, and other candidates were metadata-only. Current-open status, novelty, priority, and uniqueness remain unverified; this component earns zero verified-original or unique credit.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The p=2 spectral power mean).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Quantum/Matrix/PowerMeanOperatorRefutation.mu2`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Matrix/PowerMeanOperatorRefutation.mu2` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Raluca Dumitru; Jose Franco (2017). *On the monotonicity of weighted power means of matrices*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.07023v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For complex finite square matrices, mu2 A B t is mpow (t • mpow A 2 + (1−t) • mpow B 2) (1/2), using SpectralPower.mpow. For positive semidefinite inputs and t in [0,1], it is the positive spectral square root of tA²+(1−t)B².
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Only the p=2 operator-norm specialization).**
+
+$$claim \Leftrightarrow (\forall n: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{Matrix}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right), \mathbb{C}\right), \forall B: \operatorname{Matrix}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right), \mathbb{C}\right), \forall s: \mathbb{R}, \forall t: \mathbb{R}, ((\operatorname{PosSemidef}\left(A\right)) \land ((\operatorname{PosSemidef}\left(B\right)) \land ((0 \le s) \land ((s \le t) \land (t \le 1))))) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{opnorm}\left(A - \operatorname{mu2}\left(A, B, t\right)\right) \le \operatorname{opnorm}\left(A - \operatorname{mu2}\left(A, B, s\right)\right)))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Matrix/PowerMeanOperatorRefutation.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Raluca Dumitru; Jose Franco (2017). *On the monotonicity of weighted power means of matrices*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.07023v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The closed proposition quantifies over every finite dimension n, positive semidefinite complex matrices A,B, and real s,t with 0≤s≤t≤1. It requires ‖A−mu2 A B t‖≤‖A−mu2 A B s‖. The direction is nonincreasing in t. Every matrix norm in this statement is Matrix.Norms.L2Operator, the norm induced by EuclideanSpace C (Fin n). The full v1 all-norm assertion implies this specialization; claim does not encode that full assertion.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The matrix B).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Quantum/Matrix/PowerMeanOperatorRefutation.X`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Matrix/PowerMeanOperatorRefutation.X` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Raluca Dumitru; Jose Franco (2017). *On the monotonicity of weighted power means of matrices*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.07023v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+X=diag(1/10,4). Its first leading principal minor is 1/10 and its determinant is 2/5, so it is positive definite over C.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (The matrix A).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Quantum/Matrix/PowerMeanOperatorRefutation.Y`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Matrix/PowerMeanOperatorRefutation.Y` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Raluca Dumitru; Jose Franco (2017). *On the monotonicity of weighted power means of matrices*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.07023v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Y=[[19/50,−24/25],[−24/25,93/25]]. Its first leading principal minor is 19/50 and its determinant is 123/250, so it is positive definite over C.
+
+For A=Y and B=X, the endpoint distance at s=0 is exactly 1, and the distance at t=1/100 is strictly greater than 1. Indeed, D=X−Y satisfies D*D=I. At t=1/100 the weighted square is S=[[257/12500,−123/3125],[−123/3125,39969/2500]]. Put d=51118101/156250000, T=100051/6250, r=√d and w=√(T+2r). Positivity and (S+rI)²=(T+2r)S identify its positive spectral root as Q=(S+rI)/w. For the Euclidean unit vector v=(3/5,4/5), v*Sv=127521/12500, v*Xv=649/250 and v*Yv=399/250. The exact inequality r>57/100 gives (v*Sv+r)/w>649/250, hence v*(Q−Y)v>1. Cauchy–Schwarz and the Euclidean induced operator-norm bound give ‖Q−Y‖>1. The endpoint uses the positive spectral root of X², namely X. An entry maximum, infinity-induced norm, or Frobenius norm is never substituted.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (The specialized proposition is false).**
+
+$$\neg claim$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Quantum/Matrix/PowerMeanOperatorRefutation.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Raluca Dumitru; Jose Franco (2017). *On the monotonicity of weighted power means of matrices*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.07023v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The theorem is literally Not claim, with no additional assumptions. The witnesses n=2, A=Y, B=X, s=0, t=1/100 meet the PSD and ordered-parameter hypotheses and contradict the required nonincreasing distance. This single Euclidean operator norm is unitarily invariant, so the counterexample also contradicts the v1 universal all-norm assertion by specialization. It does not refute every norm separately or the known p=2 Frobenius statement.
+
+## References
+

+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/Quantum/Matrix/PowerMeanOperatorRefutation.result`
+- Dependency: [D5/S3/Quantum/Matrix/SpectralPower](SpectralPower.md)

+   generality: I

+import D5.S3.Quantum.Matrix.SpectralPower
+import Mathlib.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Matrix
+import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
+import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Notation
+import Mathlib.Tactic.FinCases
+import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum
+import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
+import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
+import Mathlib.Tactic.LinearCombination
+
+/-!
+The claim is the p=2 Euclidean operator-norm specialization of Conjecture 9
+in Dumitru and Franco, arXiv:1701.07023v1. The preprint is withdrawn; no
+later-resolution, originality, or priority claim is made. Its universal
+all-norm assertion implies this specialization, which is the only assertion
+encoded here. The published successor's p=2 Frobenius result is unaffected.
+
+All matrix norms use Matrix.Norms.L2Operator, induced by EuclideanSpace on
+complex vectors. The power mean uses positive spectral powers. The explicit
+positive root (S+rI)/w and a strict Rayleigh quotient give the counterexample
+X=diag(1/10,4), Y=[[19/50,-24/25],[-24/25,93/25]], s=0, t=1/100.
+-/
+
+set_option maxRecDepth 8192
+
+noncomputable section
+open Matrix
+open scoped ComplexOrder MatrixOrder Matrix.Norms.L2Operator
+
+namespace D5.S3.Quantum.Matrix.PowerMeanOperatorRefutation
+
+open D5.S3.Quantum.FiniteDimensional (QubitMatrix)
+open D5.S3.Quantum.Matrix.SpectralPower (mpow mpow_two posDef_two)
+
+/-- The p=2 power mean, using positive spectral powers on PSD inputs. -/
+def mu2 {n : ℕ} (A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (t : ℝ) :
+    Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ :=
+  mpow (t • mpow A 2 + (1 - t) • mpow B 2) (1 / 2)
+
+/-- Only the p=2 Euclidean operator-norm specialization of v1 Conjecture 9.
+The PSD hypotheses and the nonincreasing direction are retained. -/
+def claim : Prop :=
+  ∀ (n : ℕ) (A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (s t : ℝ),
+    A.PosSemidef → B.PosSemidef → 0 ≤ s → s ≤ t → t ≤ 1 →
+      ‖A - mu2 A B t‖ ≤ ‖A - mu2 A B s‖
+
+/-- The second argument B of the counterexample. -/
+def X : QubitMatrix := !![1 / 10, 0; 0, 4]
+
+/-- The first argument A of the counterexample. -/
+def Y : QubitMatrix := !![19 / 50, -24 / 25; -24 / 25, 93 / 25]
+
+private def S : QubitMatrix :=
+  !![257 / 12500, -123 / 3125; -123 / 3125, 39969 / 2500]
+private def d : ℝ := 51118101 / 156250000
+private def T : ℝ := 100051 / 6250
+private def r : ℝ := Real.sqrt d
+private def w : ℝ := Real.sqrt (T + 2 * r)
+private def K : QubitMatrix := S + r • (1 : QubitMatrix)
+private def Q : QubitMatrix := w⁻¹ • K
+private def a : ℝ := 127521 / 12500
+private def c : ℝ := 649 / 250
+private def v : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2) := WithLp.toLp 2 ![3 / 5, 4 / 5]
+
+private lemma X_pos : X.PosDef := by
+  convert posDef_two (1 / 10) 0 4 (by norm_num) (by norm_num) using 1 <;>
+    norm_num [X]
+
+private lemma Y_pos : Y.PosDef := by
+  convert posDef_two (19 / 50) (-24 / 25) (93 / 25)
+    (by norm_num) (by norm_num) using 1 <;> norm_num [Y]
+
+private lemma S_pos : S.PosDef := by
+  convert posDef_two (257 / 12500) (-123 / 3125) (39969 / 2500)
+    (by norm_num) (by norm_num) using 1 <;> norm_num [S]
+
+private lemma r_nonneg : 0 ≤ r := Real.sqrt_nonneg d
+
+private lemma r_square : r ^ 2 = d :=
+  Real.sq_sqrt (by norm_num [d])
+
+private lemma w_pos : 0 < w := by
+  apply Real.sqrt_pos.mpr
+  have hr := r_nonneg
+  dsimp [T]
+  linarith
+
+private lemma w_square : w ^ 2 = T + 2 * r := by
+  apply Real.sq_sqrt
+  have hr := r_nonneg
+  dsimp [T]
+  linarith
+
+/-- Direct two by two multiplication uses r²=det S. -/
+private lemma K_square : K * K = (T + 2 * r) • S := by
+  have hr : (r : ℂ) ^ 2 = (51118101 / 156250000 : ℂ) := by
+    rw [← Complex.ofReal_pow, r_square]
+    norm_num [d]
+  ext i j
+  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
+    norm_num [K, S, T, Matrix.mul_apply, dotProduct, Fin.sum_univ_two,
+      Matrix.one_apply, RCLike.real_smul_eq_coe_mul, smul_eq_mul,
+      Complex.ofReal_add, Complex.ofReal_mul]
+  all_goals first | ring1 | linear_combination hr
+
+private lemma Q_square : Q * Q = S := by
+  have hw0 : w ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt w_pos
+  have hscale : w⁻¹ * w⁻¹ * (T + 2 * r) = 1 := by
+    rw [← w_square]
+    field_simp [hw0]
+  simp only [Q, smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, smul_smul]
+  rw [K_square, smul_smul, hscale, one_smul]
+
+private lemma Q_nonneg : 0 ≤ Q := by
+  exact ((S_pos.posSemidef.add (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.smul r_nonneg)).smul
+    (inv_nonneg.mpr (le_of_lt w_pos))).nonneg
+
+/-- The spectral p=2 mean at the positive parameter is the explicit positive root. -/
+private lemma mean_at_t : mu2 Y X (1 / 100) = Q := by
+  have hweighted :
+      (1 / 100 : ℝ) • mpow Y 2 + (1 - (1 / 100 : ℝ)) • mpow X 2 = S := by
+    rw [mpow_two Y_pos.isHermitian, mpow_two X_pos.isHermitian]
+    ext i j
+    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
+      norm_num [X, Y, S, Matrix.mul_apply, dotProduct, Fin.sum_univ_two,
+        RCLike.real_smul_eq_coe_mul, smul_eq_mul]
+  unfold mu2
+  rw [hweighted, mpow, ← CFC.rpow_eq_cfc_real S_pos.posSemidef.nonneg,
+    ← CFC.sqrt_eq_rpow]
+  exact CFC.sqrt_unique Q_square Q_nonneg
+
+private lemma mean_at_zero : mu2 Y X 0 = X := by
+  have hXX : (X * X).PosSemidef := by
+    simpa only [X_pos.isHermitian.eq] using Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self X
+  simp only [mu2, zero_smul, sub_zero, one_smul, zero_add]
+  rw [mpow_two X_pos.isHermitian, mpow, ← CFC.rpow_eq_cfc_real hXX.nonneg,
+    ← CFC.sqrt_eq_rpow]
+  exact CFC.sqrt_mul_self X X_pos.posSemidef.nonneg
+
+private lemma reflection : (X - Y)ᴴ * (X - Y) = 1 := by
+  ext i j
+  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
+    norm_num [X, Y, Matrix.mul_apply, dotProduct, Fin.sum_univ_two,
+      Matrix.conjTranspose_apply, Matrix.one_apply, map_ofNat]
+
+private lemma endpoint_norm : ‖Y - mu2 Y X 0‖ = 1 := by
+  have hsq : ‖X - Y‖ * ‖X - Y‖ = 1 := by
+    rw [← Matrix.l2_opNorm_conjTranspose_mul_self, reflection]
+    exact norm_one
+  have hnorm : ‖X - Y‖ = 1 := by
+    apply (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg (X - Y)) zero_le_one).mp
+    simpa only [pow_two, one_mul] using hsq
+  rw [mean_at_zero, norm_sub_rev]
+  exact hnorm
+
+private lemma v_norm : ‖v‖ = 1 := by
+  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_eq]
+  norm_num [v, PiLp.toLp_apply, norm_div, Fin.sum_univ_two]
+
+/-- The exact strict scalar certificate; all square roots are positive real roots. -/
+private lemma root_rayleigh_gt : c < (a + r) / w := by
+  have hr0 := r_nonneg
+  have hr2 : r ^ 2 = (51118101 / 156250000 : ℝ) := by
+    simpa only [d] using r_square
+  have hr : (57 / 100 : ℝ) < r := by
+    by_contra h
+    have hle : r ≤ (57 / 100 : ℝ) := le_of_not_gt h
+    have hsq : r ^ 2 ≤ (57 / 100 : ℝ) ^ 2 :=
+      (sq_le_sq₀ hr0 (by norm_num)).mpr hle
+    nlinarith [hr2]
+  have hdiff : (a + r) ^ 2 - c ^ 2 * w ^ 2 =
+      -339943099 / 97656250 + (108202 / 15625) * r := by
+    rw [w_square]
+    dsimp [a, c, T]
+    nlinarith [hr2]
+  have hgap : 0 < (a + r) ^ 2 - c ^ 2 * w ^ 2 := by
+    rw [hdiff]
+    nlinarith

+# Weighted power means and a version-specific counterexample
+
+## Verified locator
+
+Raluca Dumitru and Jose Franco, *On the monotonicity of weighted power means
+of matrices*, arXiv:1701.07023v1, submitted 24 January 2017:
+https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.07023v1.
+The official source is https://arxiv.org/src/1701.07023v1.
+The final conjecture is numbered Conjecture 9 in the first-version PDF.
+
+## Source assertion and version boundary
+
+Conjecture 9 reads:
+
+> Let $A,B\geq 0$ and let $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ be a unitarily invariant norm.
+> Let $0<p\leq 2$. Then,
+> $t\mapsto\lVert A-\mu_p(A,B,t)\rVert$
+> is monotonically decreasing for $t\in[0,1]$.
+
+Here $\mu_p(A,B,t)=(tA^p+(1-t)B^p)^{1/p}$, with positive spectral powers.
+Version 2, dated 30 January 2017, withdraws the preprint because Proposition 4
+is false and major revisions are necessary. Withdrawal alone does not prove
+Conjecture 9 false. The counterexample below is
+attributed only to the displayed assertion of version 1.
+
+The published successor is Trung Hoa Dinh, Raluca Dumitru, and Jose A. Franco,
+*On the monotonicity of weighted power means for matrices*, Linear Algebra
+and its Applications **527** (2017), 128–140,
+https://doi.org/10.1016/j.laa.2017.04.003. Its author manuscript is
+https://trunghoamath.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/main-v-31.pdf.
+It proves the $p=2$ Frobenius branch and the $p=1/2$ branch for every unitarily
+invariant norm; those conclusions are compatible with this counterexample.
+This comparison uses the public three-author author manuscript. Publisher full
+version-of-record text was not obtained, so no complete comparison with it is
+claimed.
+
+No exact prior refutation was found in the bounded later primary literature
+inspected through 2026-11-01. The directly relevant *The matrix power means and
+interpolations* (2018), https://doi.org/10.15352/aot.1801-1288, remained
+text-inaccessible; other candidates were metadata-only. Current-open status,
+novelty, priority, and uniqueness remain unverified. No comprehensive
+later-resolution claim is made, and this component earns zero
+verified-original or unique credit.
+
+## Exact formal scope
+
+The closed Lean proposition `claim` quantifies over all natural dimensions,
+complex positive semidefinite matrices $A,B$, and real $0\leq s\leq t\leq1$.
+It asserts
+
+$$
+\lVert A-\mu_2(A,B,t)\rVert_{2\to2}
+\leq\lVert A-\mu_2(A,B,s)\rVert_{2\to2}.
+$$
+
+The norm is the operator norm induced by the Euclidean norm on complex
+vectors (`Matrix.Norms.L2Operator`). The power mean uses the positive spectral
+square root through continuous functional calculus. The theorem `result`
+has the literal closed type `Not claim`. This specialization follows from
+the full version-1 assertion, so its negation refutes that universal assertion.
+The formal proposition does not quantify over all norms, and the result
+does not refute every norm separately.
+
+## Exact matrices and the strict inequality
+
+Take $A=Y$, $B=X$, $s=0$, and $t=1/100$, where
+
+$$
+X=\begin{pmatrix}1/10&0\\0&4\end{pmatrix},\qquad
+Y=\begin{pmatrix}19/50&-24/25\\-24/25&93/25\end{pmatrix}.
+$$
+
+Both matrices are positive definite. Their determinants are $2/5$ and
+$123/250$, respectively. The difference $D=X-Y$ satisfies $D^*D=I$, giving
+the endpoint distance $1$. At the positive parameter put
+
+$$
+S=\frac{99X^2+Y^2}{100}
+=\begin{pmatrix}257/12500&-123/3125\\-123/3125&39969/2500\end{pmatrix},
+\quad d=\frac{51118101}{156250000},\quad T=\frac{100051}{6250}.
+$$
+
+For $r=\sqrt d$ and $w=\sqrt{T+2r}$, the matrix $Q=(S+rI)/w$ is positive
+semidefinite and satisfies $Q^2=S$, hence is the positive spectral root.
+The Euclidean unit vector $v=(3/5,4/5)$ has
+
+$$
+a=v^*Sv=\frac{127521}{12500},\qquad
+c=v^*Xv=\frac{649}{250},\qquad v^*Yv=\frac{399}{250}=c-1.
+$$
+
+The exact certificates
+
+$$
+d-(57/100)^2=\frac{88119}{39062500}>0,
+$$
+
+$$
+(a+r)^2-c^2w^2
+=-\frac{339943099}{97656250}+\frac{108202}{15625}r
+>\frac{22763263}{48828125}>0
+$$
+
+give $(a+r)/w>c$, and therefore $v^*(Q-Y)v>1$.
+Cauchy–Schwarz and the Euclidean operator-norm bound yield
+$\lVert Y-Q\rVert_{2\to2}>1$. No floating approximation is a premise.
